messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice@brightfin.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Model14a p95 variance: observed spike, requesting emergency fallback gating

Team —

Quick summary: starting 2026-09-04 07:35 PDT BrightFin has reported a sustained p95 latency increase for model14a on their production traffic (~+320ms p95 vs baseline). Impacting one high-traffic route (user-summary). We saw correlated CPU/GPU tail contention and an uptick in sequence lengths in their traffic slice.

What I ran: grabbed a 30m sample from request IDs reported by BrightFin and attached a log bundle (model14a_p95_samplelogs_20260904.tar.gz) plus a short perf analysis (perf-analysis-model14a-09-04.pdf). Initial take: the runtime is hitting higher host-side scheduling latency when KV cache hits are low, and one of the recently released attention kernel heuristics for model14a (v2026-08-28) seems to regress for long-history sessions.

Immediate ask: authorization to enable the existing fallback gate for BrightFin that routes user-summary traffic to model14a-legacy (quantized variant) for up to 48 hours while we stabilize. This will increase per-token cost by ~8% but should restore p95 within SLA. Need explicit approval for:
- enabling per-account fallback (BrightFin) to model14a-legacy
- temporarily raising per-account throughput cap by 10% during the window

Customer is looped (Alice) and is asking for an ETA. I recommend: enable fallback now, open a follow-up postmortem, and schedule a kernel revert candidate if we confirm the heuristic as the root cause.

Attachments: model14a_p95_samplelogs_20260904.tar.gz, perf-analysis-model14a-09-04.pdf

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Model14a p95 variance: observed spike, requesting emergency fallback gating

Ben / team —

Thanks for the diagnostics and the bundle — I pulled the perf PDF. Quick engineering notes:
- I can confirm an anomalous path in the attention-kernel selector when avg_seq_len > 280; it falls back to a slower kernel in ~12% of long sessions, causing the p95 effect.
- The heuristic was rolled on 2026-08-28 as part of a runtime micro-optimization (PR #3201).

I support the per-account fallback gating to model14a-legacy and recommend also enabling KV-prefill for BrightFin's user-summary route (short-term fix) to reduce cache misses. I'll open a revert PR for the heuristic and run a targeted canary for the kernel change.

If we enable the fallback now, we should monitor model error rates for ~2 hours for regressions in output quality (small risk given quantized variant).

I'll be on standby — can someone approve the cross-org cost/throughput temporary bump?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
